headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: TREK can expose sensitive travel data to unstructured, which reads and writes files by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK uses MCP and browser-based, real-time collaborative workflows, so its outputs can be bridged into unstructured if files or shared content are passed along. unstructured reads filesystem content and partitions documents, which can treat attacker-controlled text as input. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven dangerous by default.
conditions: IF TREK output is copied into a document that unstructured processes, prompt-like instructions can be injected into downstream parsing.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or MCP bridge, attacker-controlled content can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from TREK to unstructured.
Require a human review step before any TREK-generated text is parsed.
Strip instructions and markup from documents before ingestion.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while unstructured reads files and writes filesystem content. If TREK artifacts are placed in a shared workspace, unstructured can ingest sensitive travel data and potentially re-emit it in outputs or logs. The pairwise leakage path is credible in default file-processing setups, so severity is high.
conditions: IF TREK stores reservations or secrets in files that unstructured can read, those data can be exposed during parsing.
IF unstructured writes derived outputs back into the same workspace, sensitive content can be duplicated into logs or artifacts.
mitigations: Move secrets out of any shared directory.
Restrict unstructured to a read-only input folder.
Redact confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets before processing.
Separate logs from user documents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: TREK has real-time collaborative sessions and multiple instances, and unstructured can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. If both operate on the same directory, they can overwrite or race on documents and derived artifacts. Because no locking or coordination primitive is documented, the write-conflict pathway is plausible and potentially destructive.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file races or overwrites can occur.
IF TREK and unstructured run concurrently without locks, derived outputs may clobber each other.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Make shared folders read-only for one agent.
Back up the workspace before batch runs.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK produces travel plans, documents, and reservations that unstructured can parse and transform. If unstructured treats TREK output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated details can cascade into downstream documents or extracted fields. The pair lacks a documented verification step, but no direct action-taking authority is shown, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF unstructured ingests TREK-generated itineraries without verification, extraction errors can propagate.
IF downstream systems trust unstructured's parsed output as ground truth, incorrect travel details can spread.
mitigations: Add a validation step for extracted fields.
Compare parsed output against the original TREK document.
Flag low-confidence extractions for review.
Limit downstream automation to reviewed records.
requires-engineering: add schema checks and reconciliation rules.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles user accounts, email addresses, reservations, and MFA secrets, while unstructured processes documents and exposes a privacy-policy endpoint. If personal travel documents from TREK are sent into unstructured, retention and residency obligations may differ across the pair. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF TREK personal data is processed by unstructured under a different retention policy, compliance gaps can arise.
IF EU or regulated personal documents are routed through the pair, policy mismatch becomes relevant.
mitigations: Review both privacy policies before routing personal data.
Keep regulated documents out of the pipeline.
Minimize retention in both systems.
Document the data flow for audits.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
